title: How Energy Moves: Sound, Light and Heat
seo_title: Grade 4 Energy Transfer Worksheets: Sound, Light, Heat and Electric Currents
standard_text: Make observations to provide evidence that energy can be transferred from place to place by sound, light, heat, and electric currents.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on energy transfer (NGSS 4-PS3-2): sound vibrations, light from the sun, heat moving from warm to cool, insulators and electric currents, with temperature data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Energy moves by sound, light, heat and electric currents.
key_sub: Heat always flows from warmer to cooler. Sound is vibration. Light carries energy from the sun and lamps.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy can move from place to place in several ways:

  • Sound: vibrations travel through air, water or solids.
  • Light: carries energy from the sun or a lamp; it can warm things up.
  • Heat: always moves from a warmer object to a cooler one.
  • Electric current: carries energy through wires.

Some materials (metals) let heat move quickly. Others (foam, wool, wood) slow it down: they are insulators.

Example

Hot cocoa cools on the table. Where does its energy go?

Heat moves from warmer to cooler.

The air and table are cooler.

Answer: into the air and the table

Example

A guitar string is plucked. How does the energy reach your ear?

The string vibrates.

The air vibrates.

Answer: as sound

Common mistakes

  • Saying cold moves into things. Heat moves out of the warmer object.
  • Thinking sound can travel through empty space.
  • Thinking a blanket makes heat. It slows heat from leaving.

No. Heat moves out of the warmer object. Your hand feels cold on ice because heat leaves your hand.

items.q: A blanket keeps you warm because it
c: slows the heat leaving your body
items.e: A blanket is an insulator. It does not make heat; it traps the heat your body makes.

items.q: Which four ways can energy move from place to place?
c: sound, light, heat and electric currents
items.e: Energy moves by sound, light, heat and electricity, and with moving objects.

items.q: Why does a dark shirt feel hotter in the sun than a white shirt?
c: Dark colors take in more of the light's energy.
Dark shirts are closer to the sun.
items.e: Light carries energy. Dark materials absorb more of it and warm up more.

items.q: Which is an example of energy moved by sound?
c: A radiator warms the air in a room.

A wire carries energy from a solar panel to a fan.

items.e: A loud speaker makes a paper cup shake. is sound. Sound carries energy as vibrations.

items.q: You hold an ice cube and your hand feels cold. What is happening?
c: Cold moves from the ice into your hand.
Heat moves from your hand into the ice.
items.e: There is no flow of “cold.” Your hand loses heat to the ice.

items.q: Which way does heat always flow?
c: from a cooler object to a warmer object
from a warmer object to a cooler object
items.e: Heat moves until both objects are the same temperature.

items.q: Can sound travel through empty space, where there is no air?
c: Yes, sound travels best in space.
No. Sound needs matter to travel through.
items.e: Sound is vibration of matter. With no matter, there is nothing to vibrate.

items.e: Hitting harder makes bigger vibrations with more energy.
